overview: Black answers 1.d4 with ...e5 and after 2.Nf3 e4 White retreats with 3.Ng1, a reversed version of the Brooklyn idea. White has lost time but Black's e4 pawn is a target for Nc3, d3 or Bf4 and Black must support it. White gets a quiet set-up, Black a space edge. The position is rare, so the evidence is thin.

white_ideas.idea: Hit e4 with Nc3, d3 or Bf4, or play e3 and Bd3
Develop fast and aim at the weak e4 pawn
Return to a normal d4 structure after pieces come out

black_ideas.idea: Support the e4 pawn with ...f5 or ...d5
Use the extra space and attack on the kingside

typical_structures.structure: Black advanced e4 pawn against White d4
Space for Black on the e-file, chances for White to undermine

character.notes: Neither side commits to a sharp attack; the e4 pawn is the focus of play.

gambit.notes: The knight retreats and no material is given up, since the gambit is declined.

soundness.notes: Playable for both; White has lost time but nothing is refuted.

structure.notes: The e4 pawn creates a tense, undecided centre.

approach.notes: Part of the Englund family, which strong players hardly use.

level.notes: Few theory lines but the tense centre needs careful handling.
